extracted.intended_audience: nonprofit organizations, program directors, and grant writers preparing funding proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for nonprofit organizations on locating funders, preparing and submitting grant proposals, and structuring proposal components (cover letter through appendix). Emphasizes local support, eligibility, timing, budget, evaluation, and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy consistency with organization philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Is this kind of strategy consistent with our organization's philosophy?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the proposed strategy aligns with the agency's mission and core values before pursuing funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff comfort and feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Would staff feel at ease working this strategy?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess operational capacity and staff willingness to implement the proposed activities; consider training/hiring needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid duplication of existing services
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this strategy duplicate other services?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the project unnecessarily replicates local services; funders prefer complementary or innovative efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify special forms and certifications early
rubrics_metrics.description: If special forms or certification are required, this should be determined in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research funder-specific paperwork and certifications ahead of time to avoid last-minute disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect deadlines and submission timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of deadlines is extremely important because many grants are awarded only once a year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know whether deadlines are postmark or receipt, account for regional sign-offs/clearinghouses, and plan for funder cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain local support and stakeholder sign-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: Many grant programs require sign-offs by relevant local organizations affected by the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiate discussions with board members, collaborators, clients, support agencies, and federal regional agency (if applicable) and secure clearances/endorsements where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use local publicity to build community support
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective local publicity campaigns are often overlooked in planning a proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place articles/releases to inform the community and reduce misunderstanding or opposition; reviewers may contact local references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of letters of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Include only letters that are addressed to the agency director or board chairman and clearly reflect knowledge of the proposing organization, its work and track record, familiarity with proposed project, and pledge of assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague or boilerplate letters that look solicited; prefer specific endorsements that demonstrate real knowledge and commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for project continuation/renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration should be given to the problem of continuing the project or service after the initial grant runs its course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify alternative funding sources and sustainability plans (1–3 year horizon typical); discuss how the project will continue or be phased out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek expert/professional assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting expert advice can be very helpful in refining ideas and bringing credibility to your project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in-house professionals or outside consultants (fundraising consultants, state technical assistance staff, educational institutions) to strengthen proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use technical assistance and information centers
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize resources such as the Congressional Research Service, The Foundation Center, Donors Forum, Community Information Exchange, Grantsmanship Center, Support Center, and university centers for information and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage library collections, databases, seminars, workshops, and consulting services to research funders and improve proposal skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match project type to funding source (funding source selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations must know which public and private sector funders to approach for specific projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research whether funders give grants, loans, matching funds, seed capital, or program-related investments and select appropriate prospects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand government NOFA/RFP details
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register Notices of Fund Availability (NOFAs) provide due dates, contacts, legislation, objectives, allocation, eligibility, application process and selection criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review NOFAs closely to ensure compliance and alignment with program objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize government unsolicited proposal limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Government agencies generally do not accept unsolicited proposals except when set-aside discretionary funds exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the program accepts unsolicited submissions or requires applications through established processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess program status and appropriations before applying
rubrics_metrics.description: Research how much has been appropriated by the legislature and find out about application cycles or specific deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowing available funds and schedule helps target realistic request sizes and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check applicant and project eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the eligibility requirements for applicants, activities, projects? Compare these requirements with your proposed project's goals, objectives and activities for compatibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modify project scope if necessary to meet eligibility or target more appropriate funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate pre-application and agency review opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Find out if pre-applications are available and whether agency staff will review preliminary concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pre-application meetings or concept papers to get early feedback and increase competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify decision-makers and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Research who is involved in awarding grants and evaluating proposals; identify key individuals by name, location, and telephone number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding reviewers' roles can shape proposal emphasis and outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze decision factors from past awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Review previous year's awards to determine patterns—types of organizations, locations, activities, and average grant size that are favored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use past awards to infer selection priorities and tailor proposals accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the application format and submission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain the official application copy and make sure the application format is followed as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no format is provided, use a clear structure (as in this guide). Determine whether it's appropriate to contact the agency during review and learn the notification procedures for successful/unsuccessful applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research foundations and corporations before approaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn about a foundation's/corporation's past support, objectives, board relationships, geographic interest, grant application information, and financial data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use annual reports and other materials to match your proposal to funder priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific and selective when approaching corporate/foundation funders
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailor information to the company; select corporations with local presence; approach local management first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mass mailings; target funders whose purposes align with your project and leverage local recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: State whether funds sought are general operating or project-specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Make your needs known; funders may ask for specific amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about requested amounts and whether support is for operations or a discrete project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep solicitation letters brief and persuasive
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal letters should not be more than two pages; sell the organization in the first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow up with a phone call and appointment; address the letter to a named contact (avoid 'Dear Friend').

rubrics_metrics.name: Include appropriate enclosures with letters to corporations
rubrics_metrics.description: Enclosures should include copy of case statement, audit statement, board list, 501(c)(3), proposed budget, and brochures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise supporting documents that help corporate reviewers quickly assess credibility and fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid common grantseeking errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Common errors include: lack of knowledge of the donor, unrealistic demands, excessive packaging, invitations to benefit affairs, mass distribution of the same proposal, failure to follow up, and failure to use the Board of Directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research donors thoroughly, make realistic funding requests, prioritize content over glossy packaging, avoid relying on benefits for solicitation, personalize proposals, follow up, and mobilize the board's relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check submission logistics carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Check guidelines for each funder: deadlines (postmarked vs receipt), number of copies required, signatures, and simultaneous submissions to state clearinghouses for federal applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send originally signed proposals by overnight mail if necessary and request signed receipts; allow time for required regional sign-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider funder priorities, grant size, and competition in agency selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze current priorities, total funds available, size and nature of typical grants, number of proposals received and usually approved, and limitations specified in guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid requesting amounts unlikely to be funded given program size; use prior award abstracts to judge fit and competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine matching fund requirements and payment procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Many programs require recipient matching funds (cash or in-kind); government grants often use cost reimbursement and have bookkeeping requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm match percentage/type and fund transfer/payment terms before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time submissions to fiscal and funding cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider congressional/state appropriation schedules, foundation board meeting cycles, end-of-fiscal-year agency activity, and local government budgeting dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan proposal timing to coincide with funder decision calendars and to allow for sign-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate and thank agency contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivate personal contact with the staff person assigned to review projects and send thank-you notes after meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal relationships can influence review; be prepared to present succinctly and courteously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track all contacts and proposal-related communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a chart to track funding source name, address, contact person/title, letters and dates (inquiry, acceptance/rejection), appointments, submissions, backup documents submitted, site visits, decision dates, amounts requested and granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A tracking chart reduces oversights, shows follow-up history, and helps manage multiple funder prospects (recommendation: line up four prospective funders).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use simple, jargon-free language and proofread
rubrics_metrics.description: Use simple language, jargon free; avoid overusing the same words; proofread for typographical and grammatical errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the proposal aloud, set it aside and re-read, and have staff and an outside reader check for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify budget accuracy and include required organizational documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify and double-check budget numbers; attach a copy of the organization's 501(c)(3), board listing, and last audit report; include resumes, annual report, brochures, letters of support, and press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate budgets and complete supporting documentation increase credibility and reduce grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal formatting and physical presentation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Never use script type, keep paragraphs to six lines or less, use larger print type such as pica (not elite), do not use spiral binders, make sure all pages and attachments are numbered and clearly labeled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow conservative formatting to ensure readability and professional presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include ten key components in final proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Every grant proposal should include: Cover Letter; Title Page; Summary; Introduction; Problem Statement; Objectives; Methodology; Evaluation; Future Orientation; Budget; Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present sections in sequence and ensure each contains required detail; summary should be written last to reflect the distilled proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter content and signature protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letter (on organization letterhead) briefly summarizes need, proposed program, organization's qualifications, total project cost, and requested amount; signed by board chairman with executive director signing 'for the Board' if used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep it concise (preferably 25 words for initial identification), persuasive, and follow proper protocol for signatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Title page includes project title, applicant name, agency submitted to, signature, typed name and title of authorized personnel approving submission, and date of approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure authorized signatures and accurate administrative details to validate the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive summary quality and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Synopsis of project objectives, procedures, and evaluation; approximately 250 words and may be the only part reviewers read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify applicant credibility, state the need, outline objectives and activities, give dollar figures and percent of funds committed; be specific, simple, and clear; write last and make it persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: present organization background and credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Show organization's background, qualifications, and unique capability; include staff, board, affiliations, clients, volunteers, facilities, past performance, fiscal responsibility, prior funding, and need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise—highlight strengths that demonstrate capacity to carry out the project without boring readers with lengthy history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem statement: define need with appropriate evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the problem in the target area, relate to environment and impact if unaddressed; use research, statistics, previous projects, and local data; avoid exaggeration or overwhelming reviewers with data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on constituency needs (not agency concerns), use local sources primarily, include national comparisons sparingly, show knowledge of other programs, and present one optimal solution rather than multiple options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives: measurable client-centered outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: State proposed outcomes in clearly specified and measurable terms, using client's point of view and addressing what clients will look like at project conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link each objective to needs, methodology, and evaluation; categorize objectives as inputs, process, or impact; include the five essential parts: what, who, where, when, and to what extent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology: detailed activities and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe methods/activities to accomplish objectives, justification for chosen strategies, flow/timeline, target population characteristics and selection, staff requirements (hiring/training), and startup activities required before full implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about actions, sequence, duration, and why these methods will achieve objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation: criteria and data collection plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details on how the organization and funder will determine whether objectives are met, including types of evaluation information to be collected, analysis methods, and dissemination/use of findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengthen this section with evaluation criteria tied to each objective and explain how findings will inform decisions and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future orientation and sustainability plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss project's future whether limited or intended to continue/expand beyond the funding period; explain how continuation will be funded or achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe plans for future funding, scaling, or institutionalization of successful activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: fully documented and accurate costs
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of the proposed project in terms of costs; every item should be carefully documented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide line-item costs, justification, match sources, bookkeeping/payment methods, and ensure budget aligns with activities and timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix: include required supporting documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of all required support documentation deemed necessary by the funding source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach letters of support, resumes, audits, proof of tax-exempt status, brochures, and any other specified materials; label and number attachments clearly.
